chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The first thing to begin with from the wealth is the shroud, then the debt, then the bequest, then the inheritance.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for settling a deceased person's estate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the precise legal hierarchy for estate distribution, prioritizing the practical dignity of the deceased (kafan) and the rights of creditors (dayn) over the testator's discretionary gifts (wasiyya). In Shia jurisprudence, this order ensures that the physical preparation of the body and the settlement of obligations take precedence before one-third of the estate is allocated to bequests, reflecting the principle that debts are a claim on the estate similar to the rights of God. This sequence underscores the balance between honoring the deceased's immediate needs and fulfilling their financial and personal wishes.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The first thing to begin with from the wealth (legacy) is the shroud, then the debts, then the bequest, then the inheritance’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The first thing to pay for from the legacy is shroud, then debts, then will, then the shares of heirs.’”
